title: Felix Nmecha extends Borussia Dortmund contract until 2030
content:
Felix Nmecha has extended his contract at Borussia Dortmund until 2030.

Nmecha’s future at Dortmund had been uncertain. His previous contract was due to expire in 2028 and, having attracted interest from a variety of Champions League and Premier League clubs, there was speculation that he could leave Germany this summer. Nmecha also recently changed agents, again suggesting a move elsewhere was a possibility.

However, sources briefed on the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity, indicated the midfielder has committed his future to Dortmund.

Nmecha, 25, was born in Germany, but spent 12 years at Manchester City’s academy, alongside his older brother Lukas, who plays for Leeds United.

The Germany international joined Dortmund in 2023 from Wolfsburg. The move was subject to backlash from sections of Dortmund’s fanbase following Nmecha’s past anti-LGBTQ+ social media posts. Dortmund’s president at the time, Reinhold Lunow and then CEO Hans-Joachim Watzke said in a statement Nmecha had “completely convinced us during intensive talks that he does not hold any transphobic or homophobic beliefs”.

Nmecha has made 25 appearances in the Bundesliga this season, scoring two goals.

This is a very significant move by Dortmund. While Nico Schlotterbeck is their most prominent player, Nmecha is arguably their best; there are few midfielders in Europe who combine his strength and skill, and who are able to change the rhythm of a game with just a few touches.

It’s an important moment, too. Emre Can is out of contract this summer, so are Niklas Sule and Julian Brandt. The latter two will definitely leave, while Can is likely to follow them once he recovers from a serious knee injury.

In that context, Nmecha provides permanence. He will continue to attract interest, of course, and this contract extension will hardly stop that speculation, but it does buy Dortmund and protect his value. As a worst case scenario, if he does still decide to leave, the club won’t be leveraged by that dwindling contract as it enters its final two years.
